golfCartConditions: Not generally allowed on public roads. Only Class 2 municipalities may authorize certified LSVs on designated municipal streets (Ala. Code 11-73-1 to -7). Some local acts (e.g., Baldwin, Dale counties) allow golf carts on designated streets with permit, insurance, equipment, licensed driver, ~25 mph roads.
lsvRequirements: Registered LSV ($50/yr fee, Ala. Code 40-12-242.2); FMVSS 500
stateHighways: not verified
notes: LSV is local-option. Golf-cart road rules are county/city-specific; check local ordinance.

golfCartConditions: No golf-cart-specific road law found. A cart can use roads only if it qualifies as a registered LSV; local governments may designate highways (older source).
lsvRequirements: Registered LSV: 4 wheels, 20-25 mph, FMVSS-consistent equipment, license, insurance. 45 mph allowed in limited municipal/unorganized-borough cases.
stateHighways: May cross higher-speed roads at authorized intersections; municipalities may restrict
notes: Golf-cart point is from a 2020 secondary review; treat as not verified.

golfCartConditions: No statewide golf-cart road-designation statute found in this research. ARS 28-777 defines golf carts (<=25 mph, <1,800 lb unladen) for turning-yield rules; ARS 28-721(C) allows carts/NEVs on paved shoulders in specified age-restricted communities. A 2020 secondary review says carts need registration/insurance and roads <35 mph - not confirmed.
lsvRequirements: NEV: emission-free, 4 wheels, max 25 mph; cannot be driven on highways posted >35 mph (ARS 28-966); registration/insurance
stateHighways: LSV/NEV may cross at designated intersections (older source)
notes: Local ordinances (cities, communities) govern most cart use.

golfCartConditions: City may authorize golf carts by ordinance on city streets that are not state/federal highways or county roads; statute (A.C.A. 14-54-1410) limits to travel between owner's residence and a golf course; no state registration or license required for that use.
lsvMaxRoadMph: not verified (no state LSV law found)
lsvRequirements: No statewide LSV statute found (OLR 2023 lists AR as lacking one)
stateHighways: Excluded (streets that are state/federal highways or county roads)
notes: Second-hand statute text; verify on arkleg.state.ar.us.

golfCartConditions: Local authority may designate roads (CVC 21115 / 21716); roads generally 25 mph or less; golf cart defined <=15 mph (CVC 345); equipment required; license (16+) per older review.
lsvRequirements: Roads posted <=35 mph unless restricted; FMVSS 500; registered/insured; local authorities may restrict (CVC 21266)
stateHighways: Crossing at uncontrolled state-highway intersections only with state agency approval (older source)
notes: Statute pages located but text not fully read; combined with secondary summaries.

golfCartConditions: Local authority may authorize golf cars by ordinance on local roads (C.R.S. 42-4-111); not state highways; driver must be 16+; unlicensed drivers may not carry passengers <21; may cross a state highway at-grade only to continue on a non-state road; signs required before ordinance takes effect.
lsvMaxRoadMph: local option (no statewide limit; older source says 35 for LSEV)
lsvRequirements: Low-speed electric vehicle: local authorities decide; statutory equipment
stateHighways: Not allowed on state highways except at-grade crossing
notes: Golf car definition: design speed <20 mph (C.R.S. 42-1-102, per 2020 review).

golfCartConditions: Local traffic authority may permit golf carts on roads under its jurisdiction: daylight only, posted limit 25 mph or less, horn, visibility flag, valid driver license (CGS 14-300g).
lsvMaxRoadMph: not allowed - CT does not authorize LSVs
lsvRequirements: LSVs not registered by DMV
stateHighways: Not addressed (local roads only)
notes: Local towns (e.g., East Lyme, Old Lyme) add registration/designated roads.

golfCartConditions: No golf-cart road law found. A cart is legal only if it qualifies as a registered LSV.
lsvRequirements: Titled, registered, insured, plate, licensed driver; FMVSS 500; GVWR under 3,000 lb (<2,500 in 2008 source)
stateHighways: Cross higher-speed roads at intersections; generally not unincorporated dual highways

golfCartConditions: No golf-cart class, permit or designated-street authority found; an unregistered motor vehicle cannot use public highways.
lsvRequirements: LSV defined (>20-25 mph, <3,000 lb, FMVSS 500) in 18 DCMR 9901; road-speed limit for LSVs not found
stateHighways: not verified
notes: Practically, treat DC as not available for carts. Not on the 2023 OLR list.

golfCartConditions: Golf carts (<=20 mph) allowed only on county roads/city streets designated for them, posted 30 mph or less, with signs; daytime only (per statute summary); under 18 needs learner's/driver license, 18+ needs photo ID (from Oct 1 2023); may cross county road intersecting an approved road/golf course/mobile home park; local rules may be stricter.
lsvRequirements: LSV (>20-25 mph): registered, titled, insured (PIP/PDL); driver license; headlamps, stop lamps, turn signals, tail lamps, reflectors, parking brake, mirror, windshield, seat belts, VIN
stateHighways: Crossing county road at signed intersections only (golf carts); LSV may cross at intersections; local may prohibit
notes: Read from FLHSMV official page quoting Fla. Stat. 320.01, 316.212, 316.2122. Daytime-only rule from 2020 secondary review (316.212).

golfCartConditions: Georgia 'golf cart' = golf-course use only (<15 mph average). Road use is as a Personal Transportation Vehicle (PTV): local authority may designate streets by ordinance (O.C.G.A. 40-6-331); license generally required; local registration up to $15/5 yrs; PTV <20 mph. Local examples limit to roads 25 mph or less. A 2020 secondary review says 35 mph.
lsvRequirements: LSV treated as motor vehicle: registered/insured (DPS notes LSV rules under 40-6-360 to -362)
stateHighways: Local PTVs not allowed on state routes (local example); crossings per local ordinance
notes: PTV statute text read (high for local-option structure); road speed cap and LSV speed not read from statute so overall medium.

golfCartConditions: Standard golf carts not generally allowed on public roads; Hawaii County bans with limited exceptions.
lsvRequirements: Neighborhood electric vehicle: FMVSS 500, <=25 mph, registered
stateHighways: May cross faster roads at intersections; no controlled-access highways

golfCartConditions: Golf carts generally off-highway; may use public roads only where local authority permits under Idaho Code 49-208; ITD cannot title/register them.
lsvRequirements: LSV/NEV: electric, FMVSS-compliant, titled, registered, insured, licensed driver; may not cross roads posted over 45 mph
stateHighways: Crossing roads posted >45 mph not allowed
notes: 2008 OLR source said LSV limit 25 mph; newer AFDC summary says 35 - conflicting, verify.

golfCartConditions: Municipality may authorize golf carts by ordinance (625 ILCS 5/11-1426.1) after safety review; posted limit 35 mph or less; signs; licensed driver; equipment per ordinance.
lsvRequirements: Neighborhood vehicle: 20-25 mph; local permissive ordinance required for local roads
stateHighways: Cannot operate on state/federal highways; crossing of faster roads allowed (not state/federal highways)

golfCartConditions: City, county or town may permit by ordinance (IC 9-21-1-3.3); counties may allow safe right-angle crossings of state highways; licensed driver.
lsvRequirements: LSV: electric, 35 mph max (2008 source); registration per LSV rules
stateHighways: Right-angle crossing of state highways by county ordinance only

golfCartConditions: City governing body may approve golf carts on city streets (Iowa Code 321.247): licensed driver, adequate brakes, slow-moving-vehicle sign and flag, sunrise to sunset, not registered; may cross but not travel on a city street that is a primary-road extension.
lsvRequirements: LSV: FMVSS 500; registration
stateHighways: Cannot travel on primary-road extensions; crossing allowed

golfCartConditions: Golf carts may operate on city streets posted 30 mph or less; may cross faster roads; not on interstate/federal/state highways except crossing.
lsvRequirements: LSV: <=40 mph roads, may cross faster roads; registration
stateHighways: Not on state highways except crossing
notes: Work-site utility vehicles allowed to 45 mph streets; Kansas is the 40 mph LSV outlier.

golfCartConditions: Local government may authorize by ordinance (KRS 189.286, HB 154 of 2019): cart designed up to 35 mph, up to 6 people, lights/turn signals/mirrors/parking brake/seat belts/horn; posted limit 35 mph or less; no crossing roads >35 mph; sunrise-sunset; valid license; slow-moving emblem; permit/inspection.
lsvRequirements: Registered LSV; FMVSS 500 (per OLR 2023: general authorization)
stateHighways: Transportation Cabinet may prohibit use crossing state highways; no crossing roads >35 mph
notes: Read from enrolled Act text. KY golf cart definition permits 35 mph top speed, unlike most states.

golfCartConditions: Only on parish roads/municipal streets designated and signed by the local government (R.S. 32:299.4): register with OMV as off-road vehicle with decal, licensed driver, insurance, equipment; local may prohibit.
lsvRequirements: R.S. 32:300.1 LSV rules: FMVSS 500, registration, inspection
stateHighways: Not on state highways; designated crossings only, permit from DOTD in some cases
notes: Golf cart definition 25 mph (2020 review). Individual parishes/cities have their own ordinances.

golfCartConditions: No general municipal golf-cart designation statute; golf carts need a special registration permit for limited highway use or may operate on qualifying islands if the municipality allows.
lsvRequirements: Federally compliant LSV, registered, Class A/B/C license; municipalities may prohibit/restrict (29-A 2089)
stateHighways: Crossing at intersections; local may restrict
notes: 2020 review claimed local designation with 35 mph roads; the later search found no enacted statute for that. Conflict -> low for golf carts.

golfCartConditions: Unregistered golf cart only on county/municipal roads designated by the local government, posted 30 mph or less (35 at Golden Beach/Patuxent Knolls), dawn-to-dusk, lighting, keep far right, licensed driver (Transp. 21-104.2).
lsvRequirements: LSV: titled, registered with MVA, insured, licensed driver; roads <=30 mph; golf cart cannot be registered as LSV
stateHighways: LSV: crossing up to 45 mph roads at controlled intersections (2008 source); no expressways
notes: Maryland LSV limit 30 mph is below the usual 35.

golfCartConditions: Golf carts may use a public way only to travel between parts of the same golf course; owner files liability policy/bond with RMV.
lsvRequirements: Federally certified LSV: registered, titled, insured, inspected, equipped; 30 mph roads or less
stateHighways: Municipalities may prohibit on specific roads
notes: MA LSV limit 30 mph per Mass.gov summary.

golfCartConditions: Village/city/township resolution required (MCL 257.657a; townships can be disapproved by county board): driver 16+ and licensed, carts <=15 mph, roads posted 30 mph or less, may cross faster roads.
lsvRequirements: LSV (MCL 257.25b): FMVSS 500, registered, VIN; must keep as far right as practicable
stateHighways: State trunk lines: golf carts may cross; LSV state DOT may prohibit
notes: LTRC 2020 listed 15/30 posted limits - consistent.

golfCartConditions: Counties, cities, towns may permit on designated local roads (Minn. Stat. 169.045): permit-only, insurance, local ordinance conditions.
lsvRequirements: No 'low-speed vehicle' in 169.011 (defines electric and medium-speed electric vehicle); 2008 source says LSV 35 mph; local may restrict
stateHighways: Local roads only
notes: LSV rule is from 2008 source; treat as not fully verified.

golfCartConditions: Municipality may authorize golf carts/LSVs on ordinance-designated public roads inside city limits (Miss. Code Title 63 Ch. 32): license, financial responsibility, city registration/decal; roads where bicycles are legal; golf cart <=20 mph.
lsvMaxRoadMph: local option; roads where bicycles are legal (no numeric limit found)
lsvRequirements: LSV >20 and <25 mph, 4 wheels; city decal/registration
stateHighways: Not on non-interstate state/federal highways except crossing
notes: Municipality only (not unincorporated county).

golfCartConditions: Municipalities may permit golf carts on their streets (RSMo 304.034); not on state/federal highways except crossing an intersecting municipal street; no crossing where highway limit exceeds 45 mph; cities set equipment/registration.
lsvRequirements: RSMo 304.029: LSV on highways posted 35 mph or less; more stringent local rules allowed
stateHighways: Cannot use state/federal highways except crossing (<=45 mph)

golfCartConditions: Public streets/highways only where the local governing body authorizes by ordinance (MCA 61-8-391); valid license; lights/horn/mirror.
lsvMaxRoadMph: 45 for medium-speed electric vehicle; LSV/golf cart with low-speed restricted license: 25 mph roads
lsvRequirements: Medium-speed electric vehicle (MCA 61-8-377) or LSV; equipment per statute
stateHighways: Medium-speed EV up to 45 mph roads; LSV may not cross roads >45 mph
notes: Montana outlier: up to 45 mph roads for medium-speed EVs.

golfCartConditions: Only where city/village or county ordinance authorizes: sunrise-sunset, roads posted 35 mph or less, cart max 20 mph, Class O license, liability insurance (Neb. 60-6,381).
lsvRequirements: LSV on highways 35 mph or less; Class O license; liability insurance (60-6,380)
stateHighways: May cross higher-speed highways

golfCartConditions: Golf carts only on public streets specifically approved by local government; Clark County permits may be required.
lsvRequirements: Registered LSV: 4 wheels, >20-25 mph, <3,000 lb, FMVSS 500; roads 35 mph or less (NRS 484B.637)
stateHighways: May cross roads >35 mph at intersections

golfCartConditions: No standard golf-cart road authorization or local designation path found.
lsvRequirements: Compliant neighborhood electric vehicle: ways posted 35 mph or less; may cross higher-speed intersection
stateHighways: NEV may cross at intersections
notes: CityRuleLookup is a secondary site.

golfCartConditions: Golf carts are not generally street legal; only qualifying electric LSVs (N.J.S.A. 39:4-31.1 et seq.).
lsvRequirements: Electric LSV, 20-25 mph, FMVSS 500; titled, registered, insured, plated; licensed driver; '25 MPH' decal; 26-35 mph roads require DOT/county/municipal authorization
stateHighways: Crossing roads >35 mph only at signalized or approved intersections; municipalities may ban
notes: NJ LSV 25 mph default - lower than most states.

golfCartConditions: Local authorities may regulate golf carts on their streets by ordinance (NMSA 66-7-9), but not state highways; must comply with 66-3-887.
lsvRequirements: Neighborhood electric car: streets posted 35 mph or less; registration, insurance, license (66-3-1103)
stateHighways: Not on state highways (golf carts)

golfCartConditions: Golf carts not street legal unless registered as an LSV (limited-use automobile on DMV approved list).
lsvRequirements: Manufacturer-certified top speed >20 to 25 mph; 49 CFR 571.500; registered; on DMV-approved limited-use list
stateHighways: May cross faster roads at an intersection with a street 35 mph or less

golfCartConditions: Cities/counties may regulate golf carts by ordinance on public roads with speed limit 35 mph or less (G.S. 160A-300.6, 153A-245); cart <=20 mph; operator 16+; local registration/equipment/hours.
lsvRequirements: LSV: 4 wheels, electric or gas, >20 to <25 mph; roads posted 35 mph or less; FMVSS 500; registration/insurance (G.S. 20-121.1)
stateHighways: NCDOT may prohibit on any road; LSV may cross >35 mph roads at intersections
notes: Read from ncleg.gov statute text.

golfCartConditions: City ordinance may allow carts on city streets, daytime only, between owner's residence and a golf course; not federal/state/county highways except perpendicular crossing (N.D.C.C. 40-05-22; HB 1522 of 2025 may amend).
lsvRequirements: Chapter 39-29.1 LSV rules; 4 wheels, <=3,000 lb, 20-25 mph (2008)
stateHighways: Crossing only perpendicular
notes: HB 1522 (2025) status not checked.

golfCartConditions: Under-speed vehicles (20 mph or less) allowed on 35 mph-or-less streets only where local authority authorizes by ordinance (R.C. 4511.214/.215): police inspection, title, registration.
lsvRequirements: LSV (>20-25 mph) may use 35 mph-or-less streets without local ordinance
stateHighways: Not specified

golfCartConditions: Golf carts prohibited on public roads unless a city ordinance authorizes, or county commissioners approve roads posted 25 mph or less in unincorporated areas with signs (47 O.S. 11-1116).
lsvRequirements: Low-speed electrical vehicles on roads posted 35 mph or less; cities may restrict (47 O.S. 11-805.1)
stateHighways: LSV may cross higher-speed roads

golfCartConditions: Local road authority may allow by ordinance and posting (ORS 811.512 region); golf cart defined <=15 mph.
lsvRequirements: LSV: >20-25 mph, roads 35 mph or less unless city/county permits higher
stateHighways: City or county may allow higher-speed roads
notes: 2020 review noted highways adjacent to golf courses.

golfCartConditions: Golf carts may only cross highways directly (about 90 degrees) after stopping; locals can designate crossings (75 Pa.C.S. Ch. 77A).
lsvRequirements: NEV/LSV: FMVSS 500, '25 MPH Vehicle' decal; roads up to 25 mph; PennDOT/local may permit 26-35 mph (75 Pa.C.S. 3592-3593)
stateHighways: Crossings only (golf carts)

golfCartConditions: Ordinary golf carts are not street legal; 2023 H 5457 created an LSV program.
lsvRequirements: Electric, 4 wheels, <3,000 lb, >20-25 mph, FMVSS 500; registered, insured, inspected; local ordinances
stateHighways: Not specified
notes: The 2008 source said LSVs were limited to Prudence Island at 25 mph; superseded by 2023 law.

golfCartConditions: Per S.C. Code 56-2-90 (eff. May 22, 2025): registered/permitted and insured cart, driver 16+ with license, secondary highways/streets posted 35 mph or less, within 4 miles of registered address (or gated community entrance), daylight only; localities may set hours/routes/locations; children under 12 need seat belt.
lsvRequirements: LSV (56-2-100): highways posted 35 mph or less; may cross higher-limit highways at intersections; FMVSS 500; local may prohibit
stateHighways: Secondary highways only; crossing at intersections
notes: 2020 LTRC table and Justia text for old 56-2-105 were repealed; 56-2-90 statute text itself not read (SCDPS summary and bill title read).

golfCartConditions: State/county highway where posted limit is 25 mph or less (2023 amendment); faster roads - only right-angle crossing unless municipal/township ordinance; municipal ordinance must require insurance, license, permit (SDCL 32-14-14).
lsvRequirements: LSV: title, registration, LSV plate, insurance, license; not where limit exceeds 35 mph (SDCL 32-3-71)
stateHighways: Right-angle crossing of faster highways

golfCartConditions: Traditional golf carts cannot be titled/registered for road use; modified to qualify as LSV/MSV they may be registered.
lsvRequirements: Class D license; 4 wheels, 20-25 mph; FMVSS; insurance; roads 35 mph or less; medium-speed vehicles separate (T.C.A. 55-8-191)
stateHighways: LSV may cross higher-limit streets at intersections
notes: The 2020 review said county roads for modified golf carts; local rules vary.

golfCartConditions: Tex. Transp. Code 551.403: highways posted 35 mph or less, daylight only, within five miles of cart's usual parking place, and only to/from a golf course; also master-planned communities and vehicular beaches; counties, cities, TxDOT may prohibit; local authorization possible under 551.404 (not read).
lsvRequirements: LSV per federal definition; roads posted 35 mph or less (2008 source); registration/insurance
stateHighways: Crossing at intersections; TxDOT may prohibit
notes: Texas rules vary widely by city; 551.404 not read.

golfCartConditions: No golf-cart road authorization found; LSV excludes golf carts.
lsvRequirements: Titled, registered, insured, safety inspection; slow-moving-vehicle emblem; highways posted 35 mph or less (41-6a-1508)
stateHighways: Highway authority may restrict
notes: Utah has street-legal UTV/ATV law (41-6a-1509 etc.) that carts may or may not meet; not researched.

golfCartConditions: No golf-cart-specific road law; a cart is a motor vehicle needing registration, inspection, license.
lsvRequirements: NEV: electric, emission-free, <=4 passengers, <3,000 lb, FMVSS 500, 25 mph, roads posted 35 mph or less (23 V.S.A. 1043)
stateHighways: Crossing signal-controlled roads up to 50 mph if both ends are authorized NEV roads; locals may prohibit

golfCartConditions: Governing body of county/city/town must designate highways by ordinance (Va. Code 46.2-916.1 et seq.): posted speed 25 mph or less; may cross signaled intersection if limit <=35 mph.
lsvRequirements: Electric LSV, 4 wheels, 20-25 mph; local may prohibit with signs (2008 source)
stateHighways: Crossing allowed at traffic-light-controlled intersections on roads up to 35 mph
notes: Golf-cart text read from the statute. LSV details from OLR 2008.

golfCartConditions: City or county may create golf-cart zones on streets/highways of 25 mph or less (RCW 46.08.175); cart is 4-wheeled, <=20 mph (RCW 46.04.1945).
lsvRequirements: NEV: generally highways 35 mph or less (RCW 46.61.725); local may regulate; MSV class 30-35 mph
stateHighways: Not on listed state highways (NEV)

golfCartConditions: Standard golf carts cannot legally operate on public roads; factory-built LSV only.
lsvRequirements: LSV on private roads and public streets within municipal limits posted 25 mph or less; municipalities may allow some 26-35 mph roads; will not register homemade golf carts as LSVs
stateHighways: Not specified
notes: Source is a bill text and older reports; verify current WV Code 17C/17A.

golfCartConditions: Municipality may authorize golf carts on roads posted 25 mph or less (Wis. Stat. 349.18); can create crossings; not on state trunk/connecting highways except limited crossings; may allow trips to/from golf course up to one mile.
lsvRequirements: LSV: local roads 35 mph; municipalities may permit or prohibit (349.26); local-option state
stateHighways: Not on state trunk highways except crossing

golfCartConditions: Statutory golf cart (<=15 mph) is for golf-course use or authorized special events only; otherwise must be a registered Multipurpose Vehicle (MPV).
lsvRequirements: MPV: titled, registered, insured, licensed driver; slow-moving emblem if <25 mph
stateHighways: MPVs not on interstate highways
notes: OLR 2023 found no LSV law in Wyoming.
